research_protocol.ablation_policy: one disabled component; other weights unchanged; no renormalization
research_protocol.assessment_policy: same corpus, original proxy_v2 qrels, queries, and splits for every variant
research_protocol.duplicate_intent_policy: one input may have multiple milk targets; report unique input and target counts, not independent samples
research_protocol.hypothesis_policy: no guaranteed winner; no significance claim from mean scores
research_protocol.known_item_policy: count ingredient-compatible recipes as ambiguity diagnostics; do not change source-target qrels
research_protocol.spelling_denominators: candidate recall excludes curated aliases, valid controls, unknowns and unavailable targets; normalization rates include available typo targets; control rates use all respective controls
research_protocol.spelling_retrieval_metric: overlap and order against clean-query ranking, not independent relevance
research_protocol.spelling_selection: oracle selects the expected ingredient only when actually offered and available
research_protocol.spelling_status: handcrafted diagnostic examples, not a held-out user benchmark

rubric.aggregation: macro means for all queries and eligible queries within each split and scenario; binary eligibility requires grade >= 2, nDCG eligibility requires IDCG > 0
rubric.coverage_formula: shared_core / document_core_count when both core sets are nonempty

grade_rules.0: all remaining pairs; omitted from sparse qrels inside the declared corpus universe
grade_rules.1: >= 2 shared core ingredients and core coverage >= 0.30
grade_rules.2: protein match when applicable; >= 2 shared core ingredients; core coverage >= 0.45; query utility >= 0.50
grade_rules.3: protein match when query has protein; core coverage >= 0.65; query utility >= 0.60

rubric.known_item_limit: sampled ingredient subsets may match many recipes and need not identify a unique target
rubric.known_item_relevance: measure recovery of the declared source recipe only; other recipes are not judged irrelevant
rubric.latency_limit: one retrieval call per query without warm-up; descriptive only
rubric.limitations: Heuristic ingredient rubric overlaps Hybrid core coverage, query utility, and protein alignment; proxy scores measure rubric agreement, not human relevance. Corpus-derived synthetic queries do not establish real-user performance.

metric_definitions.AP@10: sum of precision at relevant ranks in top 10 / min(10, total relevant)
metric_definitions.P@k: relevant returned in top k / k
metric_definitions.R@k: relevant returned in top k / all relevant in proxy assessment universe
metric_definitions.RR@10: reciprocal rank of first grade >= 2 within top 10, else zero
metric_definitions.nDCG@k: gain 2**grade - 1 with log2(rank + 1) discount; ideal from all qrels

rubric.model_feature_limit: TF-IDF also uses titles; model differences are not algorithm-only
rubric.noisy_scenario: synthetic quantities and selected culinary aliases, not typo correction
rubric.proxy_qrel_input: clean reference ingredients; retrieval receives the original query
rubric.query_utility_formula: shared_core / reference_query_core_count when both core sets are nonempty
rubric.query_vocabulary: non-staple canonical synonym-map terms only; unlisted valid ingredients are excluded
rubric.split_limit: exact family grouping only; inspected synthetic queries are not an untouched holdout
rubric.zero_denominator_policy: score zero for all-query macro; eligible-only mean is null when no query is eligible
